title: Buffalo Cauliflower
subtitle: Roasted cauliflower in hot sauce and butter
excerpt: Buffalo cauliflower replaces the chicken with florets coated in a thin batter and roasted until crisp, then tossed in the same hot sauce and butter mixture as buffalo wings. It's really good in its own right, not a consolation version.
sourceNotes: Buffalo cauliflower emerged as a popular vegetarian alternative to buffalo wings in American restaurants in the 2010s. This recipe uses a thin batter and oven-roasting rather than deep-frying.

content.text: Buffalo cauliflower is a roasted vegetarian dish that uses the buffalo wing template: high heat, hot sauce, butter. The cauliflower is coated in a thin seasoned batter and roasted at a very high temperature until the batter sets and the florets caramelise. The buffalo sauce goes on in the last few minutes. The result is spiced, sticky, and satisfying, not a substitute so much as a related dish.

Heat the oven to 220°C (fan 200°C / gas mark 7). Line a large baking tray. Whisk together {{plain-flour}}, {{garlic-powder}}, {{paprika-smoked}}, {{sea-salt-fine}}, and {{water}} into a smooth, thin batter. Add the {{cauliflower}} florets and toss until evenly coated.
Spread the coated florets in a single layer on the baking tray, without touching. Roast for 20 minutes until the batter is set and the edges are beginning to brown.
Glaze with buffalo sauce and finish

Melt {{unsalted-butter}} in a small pan. Stir in {{louisiana-hot-sauce}} and {{garlic-powder}}. Remove the cauliflower from the oven, pour the sauce over, and toss to coat. Return to the oven for a further 8 to 10 minutes until the sauce caramelises and the florets are nicely coloured.

items.symptom: The batter slides off the cauliflower
items.cause: Cauliflower wet from washing, or batter too thin.
items.fix: Dry the florets thoroughly after washing. The batter should coat them in a thin, even layer, not pool at the base. If it seems very runny, add a tablespoon more flour.

items.symptom: The florets are steaming rather than roasting
items.cause: Tray overcrowded or oven too low.
items.fix: Space the florets out. They should be in a single layer with clear gaps. Use two trays if needed. Steam = soft; space = crisp.

items.symptom: The sauce makes the florets soggy
items.cause: Too much sauce, or sauce applied too early.
items.fix: Apply the sauce at 20 minutes and return to a hot oven. The second stage caramelises the sauce so it clings rather than pools. Use only enough sauce to coat, not drench.

items.cause: Hot sauce is mild, or too much butter in the ratio.
items.fix: Increase the hot sauce relative to the butter. A 3:2 ratio (sauce to butter) gives more heat; the standard 3:2 by volume (60 ml sauce to 40 g butter) is moderate heat.

content.text: Buffalo cauliflower appeared on American menus in the early 2010s as vegetarian options expanded. Cauliflower became a common meat substitute. It works here because it is dense enough for high-heat roasting and takes up the sauce well. Serve with celery sticks and blue cheese dip, the same accompaniments as the wings.
